ocr.notes: Some garbled words (devidediy, Aileo tas, vanqui-bed) but meaning clear.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported that St. Louis talked of nothing but the Goss-Allen fight, that sentiment was decidedly for Allen, and that sporting men believed he had been beaten by foul means but was still champion.

metadata.notes: Page header: St. Louis Dispatch, Thursday Evening, September 7, 1876. Predates the 1878 Post-Dispatch merger.

facts.fact: St. Louis opinion after the Goss fight held that the job had been set up weeks before to defeat Allen by foul means, and that he had not surrendered the championship

notes: The current summary's 'divided in favor' misreads 'decidedly in favor'.
